paper.title: Bernstein-type dimension-free concentration for self-normalised martingales

settings.name_in_paper: Logistic bandits in Hilbert spaces (responses in [0,1])
unmapped: arms lie in a closed subset of the unit ball of a separable (possibly infinite-dimensional) Hilbert space
logistic link mu(u)=1/(1+e^{-u}); responses in [0,1] with conditional mean mu(<f*,x>), not necessarily Bernoulli
settings.definition_quote: Given a closed arm-set $\cX \subset B$, the aim is to select arms $X_j \in \cX$ sequentially to minimise cumulative (pseudo-)regret, defined $R_n = \sum_{j=1}^n (\mu(\langle f^\star, x^\star\rangle) - \mu(\langle f^\star, X_j\rangle))$ ... We assume knowledge of a bound $b > 0$ such that $\norm{f^\star} \leq b$. We do not require $(Y_n)$ to be Bernoulli.

settings.name_in_paper: Logistic bandits in Hilbert spaces (Bernoulli responses)
unmapped: arms lie in a closed subset of the unit ball of a separable (possibly infinite-dimensional) Hilbert space
settings.definition_quote: Assume in addition that the responses are Bernoulli, so that $Q_n=A^\star_n$.

algorithms.name: Optimistic rule (LinUCB-style) with inflated logistic-ridge confidence ellipsoids

symbols.omega_bar: inflated confidence radius bar omega_n = omega_n(1+alpha_n) (running maximum)
symbols.gamma_A: information gain gamma(rho^{-1} A*_n) = 0.5 logdet(I + rho^{-1} A*_n), A*_n the logistic information operator at f*

conditions: confidence sequence of Theorem 4 holds with probability at least 1 - C e^{-y}
arms in closed subset of the unit ball

source.label: thm:raw_reg
source.quote: Fix $y>0$ and $\rho\ge1$. Suppose that the confidence sequence of \cref{thm:confidence-sequence} holds with probability at least $1-Ce^{-y}$ ... Then the regret of the optimistic rule above satisfies, with probability at least $1-Ce^{-y}$, for all $n\in\Np$, R_n \le 12\bar\omega_n\sqrt{\nu_\star n \gamma(\rho^{-1}A^\star_n)} + 64e^{b}\bar\omega_n^2 \gamma(\rho^{-1}A^\star_n).

results.notes: Regret defined via means, but bound holds w.p. >= 1-Ce^{-y}, so recorded as high-probability regret. Time-uniform over n. Paper's n is T, b is S.

symbols.gamma_Q: information gain gamma(rho^{-1} Q_n) of predictable quadratic variation

conditions: holds for all n satisfying rho >= C(y+iota_n)(1+gamma(rho^{-1}Q_n))
tuning: beta_n instantiated with the variance-weighted Bernstein inequality of Metelli et al. (2025)

source.label: cor:regret
source.quote: Assume in addition that the responses are Bernoulli ... Then there exists a universal constant $C>0$ such that, with probability at least $1-e^{-y}$, for all $n\in\Np$ satisfying $\rho \ge C(y+\iota_n)(1+\gamma(\rho^{-1}Q_n))$, the optimistic rule of \cref{thm:raw_reg} satisfies $R_n \le C(1+b)^6\sqrt{\rho\,\nu_\star n\,\gamma(\rho^{-1}Q_n)} + C e^b(1+b)^{12}\rho\,\gamma(\rho^{-1}Q_n)$.

results.notes: Universal constant C absorbed into O notation.

cited_results.cited_title: Generalized kernelized bandits: A novel self-normalized Bernstein-like dimension-free inequality and regret bounds
cited_results.setting_description: Bernoulli logistic bandit in Hilbert space, ||f*||<=b, high-probability regret for all n with rho >= C(y+iota_n)(1+gamma(rho^{-1}V_n))
